title: SharedMoney | Split Bills and Track Group Expenses
description: Shared expense ledger for trips and roommates. Clear balances. No bank link. Settle outside the app.
eyebrow: No bank link. No payments. Web + mobile.
heading: SharedMoney
body: Record who paid and who owes for trips, rent and dinners. No daily limits, no ads, and no bank link.
proof: No bank link or payment handling

sections.heading: A shared record beats a message thread
sections.body: When several people pay for the same plans, the hard part is remembering the details. SharedMoney keeps each expense, participant, payer, and settlement in one group record that everyone can review.
bullets: Keep settlements visible after they happen outside the app

sections.heading: Use it for the groups you already have
sections.body: Create a ledger for a weekend away, recurring household costs, a dinner group, or any other shared plan. Each group has its own activity and balances so unrelated expenses do not get mixed together.
bullets: Friends who take turns covering meals and tickets

faqs.question: Does SharedMoney handle payments?
faqs.answer: No. SharedMoney records expenses and balances. Group members settle using the payment method they prefer, then can record that settlement in the shared ledger.

faqs.question: Can groups use different currencies?
faqs.answer: Yes. SharedMoney keeps balances specific to each currency instead of silently converting them.

faqs.question: Is SharedMoney on the App Store?
faqs.answer: Yes. SharedMoney is live on the App Store for iPhone and on Google Play for Android. You can also use the web app at sharedmoney.app/app.

heading: Split bills without losing the thread.
body: Add the payer, choose the people who shared the cost, adjust the split when it is not even, and keep the final balance readable for everyone in the group.

sections.heading: Record the bill once
sections.body: Enter the cost, the person who paid, and the members included. The group can see the same entry and the balance change it created, so there is less need to explain a bill after the fact.
bullets: Meals, tickets, rides, and household purchases
A visible payer and participant list

sections.heading: Keep the settlement separate from the payment
sections.body: SharedMoney is not a payment service. It helps a group agree on what is owed; members can settle with any method they already use and add the settlement to the ledger afterward.
bullets: A record remains after the group settles

faqs.question: Can I split a bill unevenly?
faqs.answer: Yes. SharedMoney supports different participant shares, which is useful when a bill was not shared equally.

faqs.question: Do all participants need to pay through SharedMoney?
faqs.answer: No. The app tracks the shared record and balance; payment happens outside the app.

faqs.question: Is SharedMoney on the App Store?
faqs.answer: Yes. SharedMoney is live on the App Store for iPhone and on Google Play for Android. You can also use the web app at sharedmoney.app/app.

title: Free Bill Split and Settle Up Calculators | SharedMoney
description: Use free bill split and settle up calculators to work out fair shares and a simple group repayment plan before opening SharedMoney.
heading: Work out the numbers before you share them.
body: These focused tools help a group calculate a bill split or turn already-agreed net balances into a clear repayment plan. Calculator inputs remain in your browser.

sections.heading: Split a bill with fees and a tip
sections.body: Enter a subtotal, fixed fees, an optional tip, and the people sharing the cost. Use equal weights for a simple split or adjust a person’s weight when the group agreed on different shares.

sections.heading: Turn balances into a repayment plan
sections.body: If your group already knows each person’s net balance, enter the amounts to see one simple settlement plan. The tool requires the balances to add to zero and does not claim to find the globally minimum number of payments.

faqs.question: Are calculator values sent to SharedMoney?
faqs.answer: No. The calculators work in your browser and do not send bill amounts, names, or balances to analytics.

faqs.question: Do I need an account to use the tools?
faqs.answer: No. They are free to use without signing in. You can open SharedMoney if you want to track expenses over time.

title: Split Bill Calculator with Tax, Fees and Tip | SharedMoney
description: Calculate an equal or weighted bill split with a subtotal, fixed fees, tip, and up to twenty people. Values stay in your browser.
heading: Split a bill fairly, down to the last cent.
body: Add the subtotal, fixed fees, optional tip, currency, and the people sharing the bill. Choose equal weights or adjust weights for an uneven split; your values stay in this browser.

sections.heading: How this split bill calculator works
sections.body: The calculator adds the subtotal, fixed fees, and tip. It then divides the resulting total by each person’s relative weight. Any unavoidable cent remainder is allocated deterministically so the individual shares always add up to the total.
bullets: Use 1 for each person to split equally
Use relative weights such as 1, 2, and 3 for an uneven split
The total shown includes fees and tip

sections.heading: Use a shared ledger when the bill is only one of many
sections.body: A calculator is useful for one bill. For an ongoing trip, home, or group plan, SharedMoney lets the group record each expense and settlement in a shared ledger.
bullets: Choose only the people who shared each expense

faqs.question: How is a rounding remainder handled?
faqs.answer: The calculator allocates unavoidable minor-unit remainders deterministically, so every share adds up exactly to the final bill total.

faqs.question: Can I use a percentage instead of weights?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enter each agreed percentage as a relative weight, as long as all weights are positive. For example, 50 and 50 create an even split.

title: Settle Up Calculator for Group Balances | SharedMoney
description: Turn group net balances that add to zero into a simple repayment plan. Use one currency at a time and keep values in your browser.
heading: Turn group balances into a clear way to settle up.
body: Enter each person’s already-agreed net balance in one currency: positive means they should receive money, negative means they should pay. The calculator creates a simple repayment plan in your browser.

sections.heading: Read the signs correctly
sections.body: Use a positive amount for someone who should receive money and a negative amount for someone who should pay. The set of balances must total zero because every amount owed by one person is owed to someone else.

sections.heading: A practical plan, not a mathematical claim
sections.body: The calculator repeatedly matches the largest remaining payer with the largest remaining recipient. This is easy to inspect and produces a valid plan, but it is not presented as a proof of the globally minimum number of payments.

faqs.question: Why must my balances add to zero?
faqs.answer: A settlement plan is only possible when the total amount people should receive equals the total amount people should pay.

faqs.question: Does this calculator send payments?
faqs.answer: No. It creates a repayment suggestion only. Group members use their preferred payment method outside the calculator.
